prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer — it depends on what kind of place you want and what matters most to you:

- Airbnb: best for unique stays, private rooms or entire homes, lots of local/independent hosts and instant-book options. Strong host ratings system (Superhosts).  
- Vrbo: best for whole-home, family-style rentals (houses, cabins, condos) — fewer shared/room-only listings. Good for multi-bedroom stays.  
- Booking.com: best if you want hotels/professional apartments, lots of last‑minute/“pay at property” options, or flexible cancellation. Good customer service and broad inventory.

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, group size, budget and must-haves (parking, pets, kitchen, self-check-in, etc.), I can recommend which platform to prioritize and help find specific listings. Meanwhile, use the checklist and tips below to find a good host and avoid problems.

How to choose the right platform (quick guide)
- Choose Airbnb if you want independent hosts, unique places, or experiences. Look for “Superhost” and lots of recent reviews.  
- Choose Vrbo if you need a full home for a family/group and prefer owner-managed houses over shared spaces.  
- Choose Booking.com if you want professional properties, easy cancellations/pay-later, and 24/7 customer support.

Step-by-step checklist to find a reliable host
1. Filter and sort correctly
   - Set dates, guest count, whole place vs private room, and key amenities (wifi, parking, AC, self-check-in).  
   - Sort by “Most reviewed” or “Top rated” and read recent reviews. Always view total price (includes cleaning, service fees, taxes).

2. Vet reviews
   - Read the last 5–10 reviews, not just the average rating. Look for repeated praise/complaints about cleanliness, communication, and accuracy of listing.  
   - Prefer listings with multiple recent stays rather than only older reviews.

3. Check host/account signals
   - Look for badges like Superhost/Top Host (Airbnb) or high review counts.  
   - Check host profile: verified ID, how long they’ve been hosting, how many listings they have. Hosts with a single well-reviewed listing often care more about guest experience.  
   - Check response rate/time and how they answered past review complaints.

4. Check listing accuracy
   - Compare photos to descriptions. Look for clear, recent photos that show every room.  
   - Confirm exact sleeping arrangements (sofa vs bed), size of beds, and whether photos match reality in recent reviews.

5. Ask the host a few targeted questions before booking
   - Example: “Is on-site parking included? What is the check-in process? Is the neighborhood noisy at night? What’s the wifi speed?”  
   - Fast, clear, friendly responses are a good signal.

6. Watch for red flags
   - Host asks to pay off-platform (wire transfer, Venmo, etc.) — don’t do it.  
   - Vague or evasive answers to practical questions.  
   - Many cancelled reservations or few/no recent reviews.  
   - Listings with overly staged photos but no guest photos or details.

7. Confirm policies and fees
   - Read the cancellation policy, house rules, security deposit policy and cleaning fees.  
   - Check check-in/out times and whether the host charges extra for late check-in, extra guests, or parties.

Safety & payment
- Always book and pay through the platform — you get consumer protections and dispute resolution.  
- Consider travel insurance for non-refundable trips.  
- Note platform protections vary: Airbnb/others have guest refund policies but coverage limits; don’t assume everything is covered.

Useful questions to message a host (copy/paste)
“Hi — I’m [name]. Our group is [# guests, relation]. We’re coming for [purpose, e.g., vacation/work] from [dates]. A couple quick questions: 1) Is on-site parking included/close by? 2) What is the check-in process (self-check-in/lockbox/meet)? 3) How reliable is the wifi (work calls)? 4) Any house rules we should know about (noise, garbage, neighborhood)? Thanks — we’d love to book if everything checks out.”

Red flags to cancel or avoid
- Host asks to move off-platform or to sign a private contract.  
- Many past complaints about cleanliness, inaccurate listing, or rude host.  
- Host has a habit of cancelling last minute.  
- Unusual fees that aren’t explained.

After you book
- Save the host’s contact details and check-in instructions.  
- Send a short confirmation message a few days before arrival.  
- Take quick photos of the place at check-in (for safety) if anything looks off.

When to prefer which option (examples)
- Family of 4-6 needing 3 bedrooms + kitchen: start with Vrbo and filter to whole home.  
- Couple wanting a downtown apartment or unique tiny house: start with Airbnb.  
- Traveler wanting last-minute hotel-style stay with pay-at-arrival: start with Booking.com.

If you want, tell me: destination, dates, group size, must-haves, budget and whether you need flexible cancellation. I’ll suggest which platform to use and can help scan listings or draft message templates for hosts.
